brief:
Record turnout among Arab voters in Israel has triggered a political backlash and calls for investigation into what some characterize as the country's "Islamisation," according to Middle East Eye. The surge in Arab participation has reignited discussion over Israel's democratic credentials and how they are portrayed in Western media coverage of the region.

The heightened Arab engagement at the ballot box has prompted concerns among some Israeli officials and commentators, who have questioned the implications of increased minority voter participation. The controversy reflects deeper tensions over representation and identity politics within Israel's political system.
dek: The myth of Israel as the region's 'only democracy' should be dead. Not in western media Submitted by Faisal Hanif on Thu, 10/29/2026 - 15:19 Record Arab turnout has fuelled immediate backlash, amid calls for an investigation into the country's 'Islamisation'…
title: Arab voter turnout in Israel sparks democracy debate, backlash
